html:
The Battle of Aegospotami was a sea battle in the Hellespont in 405 BCE, in which a Spartan fleet under Lysander destroyed the Athenian navy. It was the last big battle of the Peloponnesian War.

Lysander's fleet was paid for with Persian money from Cyrus the Younger. He took Lampsacus on the Hellespont, the narrow strait through which grain ships brought food to Athens from the Black Sea. The Athenians beached their fleet of about 180 ships on an open shore across the water, at Aegospotami, "Goat Rivers". For several days they rowed out to offer battle and went back to forage for food. Alcibiades, who lived nearby, warned the generals that the spot was dangerous; they ignored him. Then Lysander struck while the crews were ashore and took almost the whole fleet. Only the general Conon got away, with a handful of ships. Thousands of Athenian prisoners were put to death.

Athens could no longer feed itself or hold its empire. Besieged and starving, it surrendered in 404 BCE. The Long Walls were pulled down, and Sparta set up the Thirty Tyrants.
